cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel tells it himself: the word of the LORD comes to him with a message for the shepherds of Israel. God calls him 'Son of man' and tells him to prophesy against them. And the very first word of that message? 'Woe.'
Then God asks the shepherds a question: 'Should not the shepherds feed their flock?' Friend, when God asks it like THAT, you already know how this is going.

cards.question: God's complaint is that the shepherds of Israel only feed ___.

cards.text: Then God gets specific about what the shepherds have been taking from the sheep. Friend, it reads like a RECEIPT.

cards.question: The shepherds are taking the fat, the wool and the fattened sheep for themselves.

cards.text: And then God says, 'but you do not feed the flock.' Friend, that's me baking a whole batch for the cookie boxes and eating every single cookie before the lid goes on.

cards.question: God lists what the shepherds never did for the flock. They never healed the ___ or searched for the ___.
Instead of caring for the weak sheep, how have the shepherds of Israel been ruling the flock?

cards.text: With no real shepherd, the sheep scatter. They wander over all the mountains and every high hill.

cards.question: The scattered sheep are out on the hills with no shepherd. What happens to them?

answers.text: They become food for wild beasts
They wander back to the fold

cards.question: When God's flock scatters over the face of the earth, someone at least goes out to search for them.

cards.text: Then God turns to them: 'you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD!' He lays out the charges, then hits them with that line AGAIN, and friend, when you get called out twice, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: The Lord GOD says, 'Behold, I am against the shepherds.' So what will He do with them?

answers.text: Remove them from tending the flock
Give them a bigger flock to tend
Send them out to find the strays

cards.question: Once God steps in, His flock will no longer be food for those shepherds.
The shepherds are out, but the sheep are still scattered. Who does the Lord GOD say will search for His flock now?

cards.text: God says He'll look for His flock the way a shepherd looks for his scattered sheep. He'll rescue them from every place they were scattered 'on a day of clouds and darkness.'

cards.question: After the LORD gathers His flock out of the countries, He brings them into their own ___.

cards.text: God says they'll lie down in good grazing land on the mountains of Israel, because He'll make them lie down. I spent YEARS lying under takeout menus in a junk drawer, friend, so somewhere good to lie down? Sign me UP.

cards.question: God says He'll seek the lost and bring back the strays, and the sleek and strong will get the best of His care.

cards.text: And God finishes with this: 'I will shepherd them with justice.' After shepherds who fed THEMSELVES, friend, that's a whole different kind of shepherd.
Now the Lord GOD speaks to the flock itself. 'I will judge between one sheep and another,' He says, 'between the rams and the goats.'
Turns out the shepherds weren't the only problem. Some of the sheep have been eating the good pasture and drinking the clear waters.

cards.question: Some sheep eat the good pasture, and then they ___ the rest of it with their feet.
After these sheep drink the clear waters, what do they do with the rest?

cards.text: So the rest of God's flock gets trampled grass and muddy water. That's the coworker who eats every good cookie in the break room box and leaves you the CRUMBS.
So the Lord GOD says He Himself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.

cards.question: What have the fat sheep been doing to the weak ones in the flock?
God says His flock will go on being prey.
God says He'll appoint one shepherd over His flock to feed them. Who does He name?

cards.text: That's David, who once tended sheep and became Israel's king (1 Samuel 16:11-13; 2 Samuel 5:3). God says David will feed them and be a prince among them, and the LORD will be their God.
Then God says He'll make a covenant of peace with them.

cards.question: With His covenant of peace, what does God say He'll rid the land of?

cards.text: Safe in the wilderness. Asleep in the forest. Friend, I used to jump every time somebody rattled that junk drawer open, and these sheep get to NAP in the WOODS.

cards.question: In this new picture, the showers God sends down in season are showers of ___.
God says He'll break the bars of His flock's yoke and deliver them from the hands that enslaved them.

cards.text: Fruit on the trees, produce from the land, no more prey for the nations, no more famine or scorn. God says He'll raise up for them 'a garden of renown.'

cards.question: When all this happens, what will God's flock know about the LORD their God?
At the very end, God tells His flock who they really are. Besides the sheep of His pasture, what does He call them?

cards.text: The shepherds only fed themselves, but this passage ends with God saying, 'and I am your God.' Friend, I've worn a LOT of names, and being called His beats every one of them.

findings.problem: The statement 'When God's flock scatters over the face of the earth, someone at least goes out to search for them' is false at verse 6, but it becomes true at Ezekiel 34:11-12, where the LORD Himself searches for His scattered flock. The wrong answer ('True') can be argued as right once the whole passage is in view. Tie the statement to the shepherds or to that moment, for example 'Someone goes out to search for the scattered flock while these shepherds are in charge.'

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The closing line 'that's a whole different kind of shepherd' reads like a nice dad being pleasant. It doesn't land a real laugh at the end of the stop. Push it further, or let the 'I will shepherd them with justice' moment stand on a stronger comparison.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates this stop by a wide margin. Of the 10 choice cards, 6 are multiple choice (cards 4, 7, 9, 12, 17, 18), 2 are true or false and 2 are fill in the blank. Rebalance the types.

rule.text: no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'That's David, who once tended sheep and became Israel's king (1 Samuel 16:11-13; 2 Samuel 5:3)' says that the 'My servant David' God will appoint in Ezekiel 34:23-24 is the historical shepherd-king. Ezekiel 34 doesn't say that. It only names 'My servant David' as a future appointed shepherd and prince. The card connects the passages beyond what the texts state, and it closes a question the text leaves open. Introduce him only as the text does, or say that David was once a shepherd and Israel's king without saying he is the one appointed here.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: This story card packs in more than two beats: fruit on the trees, produce from the land, no more prey for the nations, no more famine, no more scorn, and the garden of renown (Ezekiel 34:27-29). These verses are prophetic promises at the heart of the passage, not a long stretch of detail, so the card should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: 'I've worn a LOT of names, and being called His beats every one of them' adds to and changes his backstory. The backstory gives him only 'Papa' and 'Dorin' and says, 'Of every name Papa Dorin has ever been called, Papa is the best one.' Saying he has 'a LOT' of names, and that another name beats them all, contradicts that.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
